title: DAVID
text: Then David said to the Philistine, “You come to me with a sword, with a spear, and with a javelin; but I come to you in the name of Yahweh of Armies.”

body.kids: Everyone else measured Goliath against themselves. David measured him against God — and refused the king's armour because he could not move in it.
body.teens: The narrator counts everything: Goliath's height, the weight of his armour, the weight of his spearhead. David's refusal of Saul's armour rejects the terms of the contest entirely.

q.kids: What did David take to fight Goliath?
q.teens: What did David refuse before the fight?

why.kids: A sling and five smooth stones.
why.teens: He took a sling — and turned down Saul's armour, which is the theological point.

title: ESTHER
text: Who knows if you haven’t come to the kingdom for such a time as this?

body.kids: Esther was queen, but speaking to the king uninvited could get her killed. She was frightened. She went anyway.
body.teens: The book never names God. Providence shows in the shape of events — a sleepless night, a forgotten record — rather than in miracles.

q.teens: What is unusual about the book of Esther?

why.kids: Going to the king uninvited could mean death.
why.teens: It never mentions God — the providence is structural, not stated.

title: DANIEL
text: He went into his house — now his windows were open toward Jerusalem — and he kneeled on his knees three times a day and prayed and gave thanks before his God, as he did before.

body.kids: A new law said you could only pray to the king. Daniel went home and prayed like he always did.
body.teens: He does not protest, organise or hide. The witness is continuity: the ordinary practice, kept when it became costly.

q.kids: What did Daniel do when praying became illegal?
q.teens: How did Daniel respond to the decree?

why.teens: He changed nothing — neither concealment nor staged defiance.

title: MOSES
text: Yahweh will fight for you, and you shall be still.

body.kids: Moses led people who complained the whole way. At the sea, with an army behind them, God told them to stand still and watch.
body.teens: Israel does nothing at the sea. The nation begins with a rescue it could not perform, which is why grace, not achievement, is the grammar of everything after.

q.kids: What were the people told to do at the sea?
q.teens: What is the theological centre of Exodus 14?

why.kids: Stand still and watch God rescue them.
why.teens: That the deliverance is entirely God's work — Israel contributes nothing.
